questions.question: Define labour and explain the difference between unskilled, semi-skilled and skilled labour, with two examples of each. Why do skilled workers usually earn more?
questions.expected_answer: Labour is the physical and mental effort people supply to produce goods and services, rewarded with wages or salaries. Unskilled: little or no training — cleaner, dishwasher, general labourer. Semi-skilled: some training or experience — waiter, shop assistant, machine operator, driver. Skilled: high level of education or specialised training — chef, electrician, nurse, accountant, engineer. Skilled workers earn more because their skills are scarcer and take longer to acquire, while demand for them is high, so employers compete for them (return on human capital).

questions.question: Summarise five conditions of employment set by the Basic Conditions of Employment Act and the purpose of the LRA, the EEA and the UIF.
questions.expected_answer: BCEA: maximum 45 ordinary hours a week; overtime by agreement, maximum 10 hours a week, paid at 1,5 times (double on Sundays/public holidays); annual leave of 21 consecutive days (15 working days on a five-day week); sick leave of 30 days per three-year cycle; four months' maternity leave; family responsibility leave; written particulars and payslips; no employment of children under 15. LRA: right to join unions, bargain collectively and strike; protection against unfair dismissal; CCMA for disputes. EEA: prohibits unfair discrimination; affirmative action for representative workplaces. UIF: employer and employee each contribute 1%; pays benefits during unemployment, illness and maternity leave.

questions.question: Calculate: (a) weekly pay for 45 hours at the national minimum wage of R28,79; (b) the weekly pay of a waiter earning R40 an hour for 45 hours plus 5 hours' overtime; (c) net pay on gross pay of R5 000 with only a 1% UIF deduction.
questions.expected_answer: (a) 45 × R28,79 = R1 295,55. (b) Ordinary: 45 × 40 = R1 800; overtime rate 1,5 × 40 = R60; 5 × 60 = R300; total R2 100. (c) UIF = 1% × 5 000 = R50; net pay = 5 000 − 50 = R4 950 (the employer pays another R50 to the UIF).
